questions.question: Which first-time MP from Thane was named a Sansad Ratna Award recipient in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Naresh Mhaske**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Naresh Mhaske** is a prominent leader of the **Shiv Sena** (Eknath Shinde faction) who currently serves as a **Member of Parliament (MP)** representing the **Thane** Lok Sabha constituency.
 
• In **2025**, he was selected as a recipient of the prestigious **Sansad Ratna Award**, a recognition given to top-performing parliamentarians for their active participation and legislative contributions.
 
• Mhaske is a **first-time MP**, having secured his seat in the **2024 General Elections** (18th Lok Sabha) by defeating his opponent from the Shiv Sena (UBT) faction in the **Thane** district of **Maharashtra**.
 
• Before his tenure in the Parliament, he served as the **Mayor of Thane** from **November 2019 to March 2022**, where he gained significant administrative experience.
 
• The award recognizes his exceptional performance in terms of **parliamentary debates**, the number of **questions raised**, and his overall engagement in the **18th Lok Sabha** sessions. ***Hence, the correct answer is Naresh Mhaske.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sansad Ratna Awards:**
 
 
• These awards were instituted in **2010** following a suggestion by the former President of India, **Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**, to honor the best-performing lawmakers.
 
• The awards are organized by the **Prime Point Foundation** and are based on the data provided by **PRS Legislative Research** regarding the performance of MPs in the **Lok Sabha** and **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The selection criteria include factors such as **attendance**, participation in **debates**, introduction of **Private Member Bills**, and the number of **state-related or national questions** asked during the sessions.
 
 
 
• **Thane Constituency:**
 
 
• The **Thane** Lok Sabha constituency is one of the most significant political hubs in **Maharashtra**, often considered a stronghold of the **Shiv Sena**.
 
• In the **2024 elections**, the seat witnessed a high-stakes battle, and **Naresh Mhaske's** victory solidified the influence of the **Mahayuti** alliance in the region.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Rahul Shewale**: A senior leader and experienced MP from the **Mumbai South Central** constituency.
 
• **Arvind Sawant**: A veteran parliamentarian representing the **Mumbai South** constituency, belonging to the Shiv Sena (UBT).
 
• **Dr. Varsha Gaikwad**: A former state cabinet minister and current MP from **Mumbai North Central**, representing the **Indian National Congress**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Sansad Ratna Awards** are highly regarded as they are non-government awards that use objective data to promote transparency and accountability in the **Indian Parliament**.
 
• A jury committee, typically comprising eminent parliamentarians and members of **civil society**, oversees the selection process for these honors.
 
• Recipients of this award often include both **opposition** and **ruling party** members, ensuring a balanced recognition of legislative merit across the **political spectrum**.
 
• **Naresh Mhaske's** achievement as a **debutant MP** highlights the increasing focus on **new-age leadership** and active participation from first-generation parliamentarians in the **18th Lok Sabha**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a drone-launched precision-guided missile successfully test-fired by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) at a test range in Andhra Pradesh in July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ULPGM-V3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted the flight trial of the **ULPGM-V3** (UAV-Launched Precision Guided Missile - Version 3) in **July 2025**.
 
• The test was carried out at a specialized defense range in **Andhra Pradesh**, aimed at validating the missile's **guidance system** and its ability to engage targets from **unmanned platforms**.
 
• The **ULPGM-V3** is a lightweight, high-precision missile designed to be integrated into **UAVs** (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) to enhance their **offensive strike capabilities** against ground-based assets.
 
• Equipped with an advanced **Imaging Infrared (IIR) seeker**, the missile can perform surgical strikes against both **stationary and moving targets**, including enemy **tanks**, **command centers**, and **armoured personnel carriers**.
 
• The successful development of this missile represents a significant leap in indigenous **aerial combat technology**, aligning with the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative to modernize the **Indian Armed Forces** with home-grown equipment. ***Hence, the correct answer is ULPGM-V3.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Astra Mk-II:**
 
 
• The **Astra Mk-II** is an advanced **Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air Missile (BVRAAM)**.
 
• It is designed to engage enemy **aircraft** at long distances, with an estimated range of approximately **160 kilometres**.
 
• The missile utilizes **active radar homing** and is a successor to the **Astra Mk-I**, which is already inducted into the **Indian Air Force (IAF)**.
 
 
 
• **Agni-P (Agni-Prime):**
 
 
• The **Agni-P** is a new-generation **nuclear-capable ballistic missile** developed by **DRDO**.
 
• It is a **two-stage canisterized** solid propellant missile with a range capability between **1,000 and 2,000 kilometres**.
 
• The **canisterized system** ensures that the missile can be stored for long periods and transported easily via **rail or road**, significantly improving its **operational readiness**.
 
 
 
• **Nirbhay-V3:**
 
 
• **Nirbhay** is India’s first indigenous **long-range subsonic cruise missile**.
 
• It is capable of carrying **nuclear and conventional warheads** and has a strike range of over **1,000 kilometres**.
 
• The missile is known for its **terrain-hugging** capability, allowing it to fly at very low altitudes to evade **enemy radar systems**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **DRDO Background:** The **Defence Research and Development Organisation** was established in **1958** by merging the **Technical Development Establishment** and the **Directorate of Technical Development and Production**. It functions under the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
• **UAV Integration:** The **ULPGM** series is vital for arming indigenous drones like the **Tapus-BH-201** (MALE UAV) and the **Archer-NG**, providing them with a lethal **stand-off strike** capability.
 
• **Precision Strike Technology:** The use of **laser-guided** or **IIR seekers** in missiles like **ULPGM-V3** minimizes **collateral damage** and ensures a high **probability of kill (Pk)** in complex battlefield environments.
 
• **Strategic Significance:** Developing drone-launched missiles locally reduces the dependency on foreign systems like the American **Hellfire** or the Turkish **MAM-L** missiles.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following organization’s main purpose is collective defence, meaning an attack on one member is considered an attack on all?

options.text: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)** is an intergovernmental **military alliance** established by the **North Atlantic Treaty** (also known as the **Washington Treaty**) signed on **4 April 1949**.
 
• The core principle of NATO is **collective defence**, which is enshrined in **Article 5** of its founding treaty. This article states that an **armed attack against one or more** of its members in Europe or North America shall be **considered an attack against them all**. ***Hence, the correct answer is North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).***
 
• The primary purpose of the alliance is to **safeguard the freedom and security** of its member countries through **political and military means**. Politically, it promotes democratic values, while militarily, it is committed to the peaceful resolution of disputes.
 
• NATO was originally formed by **12 founding members**, including the **United States, Canada, United Kingdom, France, and Italy**, primarily to provide collective security against the threat posed by the **Soviet Union** during the **Cold War** era.
 
• Under the collective defence mechanism, if a member state is attacked, every other member is obligated to assist the party attacked, which may include the **use of armed force** to restore and maintain the security of the North Atlantic area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO):**
 
 
• The **WTO** is the only global international organization dealing with the **rules of trade between nations**.
 
• It was established on **1 January 1995** following the **Marrakesh Agreement**, replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).
 
• Its headquarters is located in **Geneva, Switzerland**. Its main function is to ensure that **trade flows as smoothly, predictably, and freely** as possible.
 
 
 
• **World Health Organization (WHO):**
 
 
• The **WHO** is a specialized agency of the **United Nations** responsible for **international public health**.
 
• It was founded on **7 April 1948** (celebrated as **World Health Day**) and is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**.
 
• Its mandate includes advocating for **universal healthcare**, monitoring public health risks, and coordinating responses to **health emergencies**.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization):**
 
 
• **UNESCO** aims to build peace through **international cooperation** in **Education, the Sciences, and Culture**.
 
• It was founded on **16 November 1945** and its headquarters is located in **Paris, France**.
 
• It is well known for designating **World Heritage Sites** to preserve cultural and natural heritage around the globe.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts about NATO:**
 
 
• The **headquarters** of NATO is located in **Brussels, Belgium**.
 
• As of **2024**, NATO consists of **32 member countries**, with **Finland** and **Sweden** being the most recent additions to the alliance.
 
• **Article 5** has been invoked only **once** in the history of the alliance, which was in response to the **September 11, 2001**, terrorist attacks on the **United States**.
 
• The current **Secretary General** of NATO (as of 2024) is **Mark Rutte**, who succeeded Jens Stoltenberg.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In November 2025, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) implemented Stage‑II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi‑NCR. Which air quality category and AQI range did this stage correspond to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Very Poor (AQI 301–400)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)** in **National Capital Region (NCR)** and Adjoining Areas is the statutory body responsible for implementing the **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)** to combat air pollution.
 
• **Stage-II** of the **GRAP** is specifically invoked when the **Air Quality Index (AQI)** in **Delhi-NCR** is forecast to or has already reached the **'Very Poor'** category, which spans a numerical range of **301 to 400**.
 
• In **November 2025**, the implementation of **Stage-II** necessitated restrictive measures to prevent further deterioration of air quality toward the **'Severe'** category. ***Hence, the correct answer is Very Poor (AQI 301–400).***
 
• Under this stage, the use of **Diesel Generator (DG) sets** is heavily regulated and generally banned except for essential services like hospitals and elevators to minimize **vehicular and industrial emissions**.
 
• Other mandatory actions under **Stage-II** include the mechanical sweeping and **water sprinkling** of identified roads on a daily basis and the intensification of inspections at **construction and demolition (C&D) sites**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP):**
 
 
• It is a set of emergency measures that kick in to prevent further deterioration of air quality in **Delhi-NCR**. It was first notified in **2017** by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**.
 
• The plan is divided into four stages based on the **AQI** levels:
 
 
• **Stage-I ('Poor'):** Triggered when **AQI** is between **201–300**. Focuses on dust control at construction sites and waste management.
 
• **Stage-II ('Very Poor'):** Triggered when **AQI** is between **301–400**. Focuses on **DG set** restrictions and increasing parking fees.
 
• **Stage-III ('Severe'):** Triggered when **AQI** is between **401–450**. Includes bans on non-essential construction and specific vehicle types (e.g., **BS-III petrol** and **BS-IV diesel** cars).
 
• **Stage-IV ('Severe+'):** Triggered when **AQI** exceeds **450**. This involves stopping the entry of trucks into **Delhi** and potentially shifting schools to online mode.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM):**
 
 
• The **CAQM** was established through an **Ordinance in 2020** and later by the **CAQM in NCR and Adjoining Areas Act, 2021**.
 
• It replaced the **Environment Pollution (Prevention and Control) Authority (EPCA)** and has the power to issue directions and entertain complaints for protecting and improving air quality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Forecasting Mechanism:** The decision to invoke stages of **GRAP** is based on forecasts provided by the **Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM)** and the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)**.
 
• **Pollutants Monitored:** The **AQI** calculation involves eight major pollutants: **PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, and Pb**. However, **PM2.5** and **PM10** are the primary concerns in **Delhi** during the winter months of **October and November**.
 
• **Geographical Scope:** **GRAP** measures are applicable across the entire **National Capital Region**, which includes districts in **Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan**, besides **Delhi**.
 
• **Public Participation:** During **Stage-II**, citizens are encouraged to use **public transport** (Metro and buses) and minimize the use of personal vehicles to reduce the **carbon footprint** and local pollution levels.

questions.question: In November 2025, which of the following government bodies expressed serious concern over Delhi’s deteriorating air quality, stating that even wearing masks had become ineffective?

options.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2025**, the **Supreme Court of India** expressed grave concern over the "severe plus" **Air Quality Index (AQI)** levels in **Delhi** and the **National Capital Region (NCR)**.
 
• A bench comprising **Justice Abhay S. Oka** and **Justice Augustine George Masih** observed that the pollution levels had reached a stage where even wearing **masks** was becoming ineffective for the citizens.
 
• The **Supreme Court** pulled up the **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)** for the delay in implementing the **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)**, specifically **Stage IV** measures.
 
• The court invoked **Article 21** of the **Constitution of India**, asserting that every citizen has a fundamental right to live in a **pollution-free environment**.
 
• The **Supreme Court** directed all **NCR states** to immediately constitute teams to monitor and enforce the **GRAP-IV** restrictions, which include a ban on **truck entry** (except for essential commodities) and the suspension of **construction and demolition activities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP):**
 
 
• **GRAP** is a set of emergency measures implemented in **Delhi-NCR** depending on the severity of air pollution.
 
• It is divided into four stages: **Stage I (Poor)**, **Stage II (Very Poor)**, **Stage III (Severe)**, and **Stage IV (Severe Plus)**.
 
• **Stage IV** is triggered when the **AQI** crosses the **450 mark**, involving the strictest curbs like stopping the entry of non-essential commercial vehicles into **Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM):**
 
 
• The **CAQM** is a statutory body established under the **Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas Act, 2021**.
 
• It was formed to coordinate and oversee efforts to improve air quality in **Delhi-NCR** and adjoining states like **Punjab**, **Haryana**, **Rajasthan**, and **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
 
 
• **Primary Pollutants:**
 
 
• The crisis is often exacerbated by **PM2.5** and **PM10** particles, which can penetrate deep into the lungs.
 
• Key contributors to **Delhi's** air pollution in **November** include **stubble burning** (parali burning) in neighboring states, **vehicular emissions**, **construction dust**, and **low wind speeds** due to winter temperature inversion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Supreme Court** clarified that even if the **AQI** falls below **450**, the **GRAP-IV** restrictions should not be relaxed without the court's prior permission during the peak pollution season.
 
• The **National Air Quality Index** was launched in **2014** as part of the **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** to provide a simplified "one number-one color-one description" for the general public to understand air quality.
 
• Other bodies involved in pollution control include the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, established in **1974**, which provides technical services to the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**.
</ul

questions.question: In March 2025, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change conducted a national-level workshop on the National Adaptation Plan on Climate Change at ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** organized a national-level workshop in **March 2025** to discuss and refine the **National Adaptation Plan (NAP)** of India.
 
• The workshop was held in **New Delhi**, serving as a central hub for policy-makers, climate scientists, and international delegates to deliberate on **climate resilience** strategies.
 
• The primary objective of the event was to strengthen the framework for **climate change adaptation** at both national and state levels, aligning with India's commitments under the **Paris Agreement**.
 
• The workshop emphasized the integration of **traditional knowledge** with modern **scientific data** to protect vulnerable communities from extreme weather events like **floods, droughts, and heatwaves**.
 
• It facilitated a platform for **State Governments** to share their progress on **State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCC)** and identify gaps in funding and technology transfer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC):**
 
 
• Launched in **June 2008**, the **NAPCC** is India's flagship strategy to address climate change through **eight core national missions**.
 
• These missions include the **National Solar Mission**, **National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency**, and the **National Mission on Sustainable Habitat**.
 
• Other critical components include the **National Water Mission**, **National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem**, and **National Mission for a Green India**.
 
• The **National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture** and the **National Mission on Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change** complete the framework.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC):**
 
 
• It is the **nodal agency** in the **Government of India** for planning, promotion, coordination, and overseeing the implementation of environmental and forestry programmes.
 
• The ministry is responsible for India's participation in international bodies like the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)** and the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**.
 
 
 
• **State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC):**
 
 
• Individual **States and Union Territories** in India develop their own **SAPCCs** to address region-specific climate vulnerabilities.
 
• These plans are periodically updated to reflect **Intended Nationally Determined Contributions (INDCs)** and **Net Zero** goals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC):**
 
 
• Established in **2015-16**, this fund assists states that are particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change in meeting the cost of **adaptation**.
 
• The **NABARD** acts as the **National Implementing Entity (NIE)** for projects under this fund.
 
 
 
• **India's Climate Targets:**
 
 
• During **COP26** in **Glasgow**, India announced the **Panchamrit** targets, which include achieving **Net Zero emissions by 2070**.
 
• India also aims to increase its **non-fossil energy capacity** to **500 GW by 2030**.
 
• The **National Adaptation Plan** discussed in the **New Delhi** workshop is a crucial step in ensuring that developmental gains are not reversed by **climate-induced disasters**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Where in Andhra Pradesh was the Rajiv Sports Complex, developed by Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC), inaugurated in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gajuwaka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rajiv Sports Complex** was officially inaugurated in **June 2025** to enhance the sporting infrastructure and provide better facilities for athletes in the region.
 
• The complex is situated in **Gajuwaka**, which is one of the most prominent residential and industrial suburbs of **Visakhapatnam**, **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The development of this project was undertaken by the **Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC)**, aiming to promote physical fitness among the local youth and industrial workers.
 
• The facility includes state-of-the-art amenities such as **shuttle badminton courts**, **multipurpose halls**, **gymnasiums**, and dedicated spaces for **indoor games**.
 
• The strategic location in **Gajuwaka** allows easy access for the massive population working in nearby industrial zones like the **Visakhapatnam Steel Plant** and **BHEL**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC):**
 
 
• The **GVMC** is the civic body that oversees the administration of **Visakhapatnam**. It is one of the largest municipal corporations in **India** by area, covering approximately **681.96 square kilometers**.
 
• It has been instrumental in implementing various **Smart City** projects, focusing on urban greenery, waste management, and public sports facilities.
 
 
 
• **Gajuwaka Locality:**
 
 
• **Gajuwaka** is often referred to as the biggest shopping hub in the **Andhra Pradesh** state and serves as a vital economic engine for the city of **Visakhapatnam**.

questions.question: Which Canadian province held the G7 Summit in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alberta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **51st G7 Summit** is scheduled to be hosted by **Canada** in **June 2025**.
 
• The government of **Canada** has officially designated the province of **Alberta** as the host region for this high-profile international gathering.
 
• Specifically, the summit will take place in **Kananaskis**, a scenic area located in the foothills of the **Canadian Rockies** within **Alberta**.
 
• Prime Minister **Justin Trudeau** announced the selection of **Alberta** to highlight the province's natural beauty and its vital role in the national economy. ***Hence, the option Alberta is correct.***
 
• This will be the **seventh time** that **Canada** has hosted the **G7 Summit** since it joined the group in **1976**.
 
• The **G7 Presidency** for the year **2025** belongs to **Canada**, which takes over the leadership role from **Italy** (the **2024** host).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographic Importance of Alberta:**
 
 
• **Alberta** is one of the three prairie provinces in **Western Canada** and is bordered by **British Columbia** to the west and **Saskatchewan** to the east.
 
• It is home to major cities such as **Calgary** and the provincial capital, **Edmonton**.
 
• The province is globally recognized for its **oil and natural gas** industry, as well as its stunning national parks like **Banff** and **Jasper**.
 
 
 
• **History of G7 in Canada:**
 
 
• **Canada** previously hosted the summit in several locations: **Ottawa-Montebello (1981)**, **Toronto (1988)**, **Halifax (1995)**, **Kananaskis (2002)**, **Muskoka (2010)**, and **Charlevoix (2018)**.
 
• The choice of **Kananaskis** in **2025** mirrors the **2002** summit, which was chosen for its remote and secure location, facilitating focused discussions among world leaders.
 
 
 
• **Member Countries:**
 
 
• The **Group of Seven (G7)** is an intergovernmental political forum consisting of **Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States**.
 
• The **European Union** is also represented at the summit as a non-enumerated member, participating in all discussions.

questions.question: In January 2025, which of the following expanded its Sandbox Framework to support innovation in the insurance sector?

options.text: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** announced the expansion of its **Regulatory Sandbox Framework** to foster greater **innovation** and **technological advancement** within the insurance industry.
 
• The primary objective of this expansion is to provide a "safe space" for **InsurTech** companies and traditional insurers to test new **products**, **services**, and **business models** in a live environment with certain **regulatory relaxations**.
 
• The revised framework aims to accelerate the goal of **"Insurance for All by 2047"** by encouraging solutions that address the needs of **unserved** and **underserved** segments of the **Indian population**.
 
• This expansion includes streamlined **application processes** and extended **testing timelines**, allowing participants more flexibility to refine their **innovations** before a full-scale market launch.
 
• By leveraging the sandbox, **IRDAI** seeks to promote the use of **emerging technologies** such as **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Machine Learning**, and **Blockchain** to improve **policy issuance** and **claims settlement** efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India):**
 
 
• It is a **statutory body** established under the **IRDAI Act, 1999**, following the recommendations of the **Malhotra Committee** report.
 
• The authority is headquartered in **Hyderabad** (shifted from **Delhi** in **2001**) and functions under the jurisdiction of the **Ministry of Finance**.
 
• The current Chairperson of **IRDAI** is **Debasish Panda**, who leads the mission of protecting **policyholders' interests** and ensuring the **orderly growth** of the insurance sector.
 
 
 
• **Other Regulatory Sandboxes in India:**
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** operates a **Regulatory Sandbox** focused on **FinTech** themes such as **retail payments**, **MSME lending**, and **cross-border remittances**.
 
• The **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** manages a sandbox for the **capital markets**, enabling innovations in **trading platforms** and **investment advisory** services.
 
• The **International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA)** also maintains a sandbox specifically for **global financial innovations** within **GIFT City, Gujarat**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Sandbox Definition:**
 
 
• A **Regulatory Sandbox** refers to live, **time-bound testing** of new products or services in a **controlled regulatory environment**.
 
• It allows regulators to understand **new technologies** and their **risks** without immediately imposing the full weight of **existing regulations**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **IRDAI** Sandbox was originally introduced in **2019**, and the **January 2025** update represents a move toward a more **permanent** and **dynamic** regulatory approach.
 
• Key areas of interest for the **2025 expansion** include **Parametric Insurance** (weather-based covers), **Telematic-based motor insurance** (pay-as-you-drive), and **Wearable-integrated health insurance**.
 
• Any entity registered in **India**, including **startups** and **intermediaries**, can apply to participate, provided they meet the **minimum net worth** and **innovation criteria** set by the regulator.
 
• Successful testing within the sandbox often leads to the **amendment** of existing **insurance laws** to accommodate modern **digital-first** insurance solutions.
</ul

questions.question: In which forest region of Kerala were seven new moth species recorded for the first time in 2025 by a team of entomologists?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ranipuram forest**__.

__
 
• In **2025**, a team of dedicated **entomologists** from institutions such as **Christ College (Irinjalakuda)** conducted a comprehensive survey in the **Ranipuram forest** region of **Kerala**.
 
• During this scientific expedition, the researchers successfully recorded **seven new moth species** that had never been documented in the state of **Kerala** before.
 
• The **Ranipuram forest**, located in the **Kasaragod district**, is part of the **Western Ghats**, which is a global **biodiversity hotspot** and a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The discovery includes species from diverse families such as **Erebidae** and **Noctuidae**, highlighting the rich lepidopteran diversity of the northern **Western Ghats**.
 
• This finding underscores the ecological importance of the **high-altitude shola-grassland** ecosystems found in the **Kasaragod** region for rare and endemic insect life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ranipuram Forest:**
 
 
• Located in the **Kasaragod district** of **Kerala**, it was formerly known as **Madathumala**.
 
• It is often referred to as the **"Ooty of Kerala"** due to its cool climate and scenic beauty, situated at an elevation of about **1022 meters**.
 
• The landscape is a unique blend of **evergreen forests**, **shola woods**, and **montane grasslands**, which supports a wide array of **flora and fauna**.
 
• It borders the **Talakavery Wildlife Sanctuary** in **Karnataka**, forming an important corridor for elephants and other wildlife.
 
 
 
• **Moths as Bioindicators:**
 
 
• Moths belong to the order **Lepidoptera** and are considered excellent **bioindicators** because they are highly sensitive to changes in the environment and climate.
 
• Unlike butterflies, most moths are **nocturnal**, and their diversity reflects the health of the local **ecosystem** and the availability of specific host plants.
 
 
 
• **Other Regions Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Silent Valley National Park:** Located in **Palakkad**, famous for the **Lion-tailed Macaque** and its untouched tropical rainforest.
 
• **Periyar Tiger Reserve:** Situated in **Idukki**, it is one of the most prominent **Tiger** and **Elephant** reserves in **India**.
 
• **Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary:** Part of the **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve**, known for its significant population of **Tigers** and **Asian Elephants**.

• The survey methodology involved the use of **mercury vapor lamp light traps** to attract and document the **nocturnal insect** species.
 
• Taxonomic studies and **DNA barcoding** are often used by entomologists to confirm the identity of such rare species in the **Western Ghats**.
 
• The **Government of Kerala** and various **nature conservation foundations** have been emphasizing the protection of the **Ranipuram-Kottancheri** belt to prevent habitat fragmentation.
 
• The year **2025** marks a significant milestone in the **entomological research** of North Kerala, bringing global attention to the lesser-explored forest tracts of the **Kasaragod** highlands.
</ul

questions.question: In April 2024, the Indian Space Research Organisation's (ISRO) Chairman, S Somanath, made a declaration to achieve debris-free space missions by the year _____.
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**2030**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **42nd Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee (IADCC)** annual meeting held in **April 2024** in **Bengaluru**, the **ISRO** Chairman, **S Somanath**, declared India's commitment to achieving **debris-free space missions** by the year **2030**.
 
• This initiative is part of **ISRO's** broader vision to ensure the **long-term sustainability** of outer space operations, preventing the accumulation of "space junk" that could jeopardize future missions.
 
• The goal of a **Debris-free Space Mission** involves all Indian space actors, including both **government-led projects** and **private sector** startups, ensuring that every mission launched from India leaves no debris behind in the **Earth's orbit**.
 
• The **ISRO** Chairman emphasized that by **2030**, India aims to have a well-defined mechanism to de-orbit satellites at the end of their functional life or ensure their natural decay within a specified timeframe.
 
• This declaration reinforces India's position as a responsible global space power, actively contributing to the **United Nations** guidelines for space debris mitigation and the **IADCC** framework. ***Hence, the correct option is 2030.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Space Debris and its Risks:** 
 
 
• Space debris refers to **man-made objects** in orbit that no longer serve a useful function, such as **defunct satellites**, spent **rocket stages**, and fragments from collisions.
 
• The **Kessler Syndrome** is a theoretical scenario where the density of objects in **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)** is high enough that collisions between objects could cause a cascade, making space activities and the use of satellites difficult for generations.
 
 
 
• **ISRO's Technological Interventions:** 
 
 
• **IS4OM (ISRO System for Safe and Sustainable Space Operations Management)**: This facility was established in **July 2022** to monitor space objects, predict collisions, and coordinate debris mitigation activities.
 
• **POEM (PSLV Orbital Experimental Module)**: **ISRO** has successfully utilized the **fourth stage (PS4)** of the **PSLV** rocket as an orbital platform for experiments, rather than letting it become debris immediately. In **March 2024**, the **PSLV-C58** POEM-3 mission achieved a zero-debris status by re-entering the atmosphere.
 
• **SPADEX (Space Docking Experiment)**: A mission currently under development aimed at mastering **autonomous docking**, which is crucial for **satellite servicing** and debris removal.
 
 
 
• **IADCC (Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee):** 
 
 
• It is an international governmental forum for the worldwide coordination of activities related to the issues of **man-made** and **natural debris** in space.
 
• The **42nd** meeting hosted by **ISRO** in **Bengaluru** saw participation from various global space agencies like **NASA**, **ESA**, and **JAXA**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Future Landmarks for ISRO:** 
 
 
• While the debris-free target is **2030**, India has other major milestones including the establishment of the **Bhartiya Antariksha Station (BAS)** by **2035**.
 
• India also plans to send the first Indian to the **Moon** by the year **2040**.
 
• The **Gaganyaan** mission, India's first **manned space flight**, is a critical step toward these goals, requiring a clean and safe orbital environment.
 
 
 
• **Global Compliance:** 
 
 
• India's commitment aligns with the **Zero Debris Charter** and the **Space Sustainability** goals discussed at international platforms to keep **Low Earth Orbit** accessible for future **scientific and commercial** use.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: As per Union Budget 2025-26, under the new income tax regime, what is the tax-exempt income threshold?

• In the **Union Budget 2025-26**, presented by Union Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman**, the government announced a significant increase in the tax-exempt income threshold under the **New Tax Regime**.

• This change is implemented through a combination of revised **Income Tax Slabs** and the **Tax Rebate** under **Section 87A** of the **Income Tax Act**.
 
• The **Standard Deduction** for salaried employees has been increased from **₹75,000** to **₹1,00,000** in the **FY 2025-26** budget.
 
• The primary objective of this move is to provide substantial relief to the **middle-class taxpayers** and increase disposable income in the hands of the public.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Revised Tax Slabs (Budget 2025-26):**
 
 
• **₹0 to ₹4 lakh**: Nil tax.
 
• **₹4 lakh to ₹8 lakh**: **5%** tax.
 
• **₹8 lakh to ₹12 lakh**: **10%** tax.
 
• **₹12 lakh to ₹16 lakh**: **15%** tax.
 
• **₹16 lakh to ₹20 lakh**: **20%** tax.
 
• **Above ₹24 lakh**: **30%** tax.
 
 
 
• **Section 87A Rebate:** This section provides a **tax rebate** that effectively makes the tax liability zero for those whose total income does not exceed the specified threshold. In the **Budget 2025-26**, this rebate was adjusted to cover income up to **₹12 lakh**.

• **Pensioners' Relief:** The deduction on **family pension** for pensioners has been enhanced from **₹25,000** to **₹30,000** to provide further social security benefits.

• **Impact on Taxpayers:** Under the new structure, a salaried individual earning **₹12 lakh** per annum will pay **zero tax**, leading to a direct saving compared to previous fiscal years where the limit was lower.
 
• **Surcharge and Cess:** While the tax rates have been rationalized, the **Health and Education Cess** of **4%** remains applicable on the total tax amount for those above the rebate threshold.
 
• **Corporate Tax:** The **Budget 2025-26** also maintained the stability of corporate tax rates, focusing on the **Ease of Doing Business** and simplifying the **Tax Assessment** process.
 
• **Date of Implementation:** These changes are applicable for the **Assessment Year 2026-27** (which corresponds to the **Financial Year 2025-26** starting from **1 April 2025**).

questions.question: Which Constitutional Articles did earlier Supreme Court judgements connect manual scavenging to, as a violation in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 17 and 21**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Supreme Court** of India, in its observations leading up to **February 2025**, has reaffirmed that the practice of **manual scavenging** is a direct violation of **Article 17** and **Article 21** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• **Article 17** of the Constitution abolished "**Untouchability**" and forbade its practice in any form. The Court has historically noted that **manual scavenging** is a dehumanizing practice rooted in the caste system, effectively serving as a modern manifestation of untouchability.
 
• **Article 21** guarantees the **Protection of Life and Personal Liberty**. The judiciary has interpreted this to include the **right to live with dignity**. Forcing individuals to handle human excreta manually is considered a gross violation of this fundamental right to a dignified life.
